title: Quaternion Gaussian Probes for Tensor Frobenius-Norm Estimation
authors: Yannan Chen, Hailin Sun, Min Xi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12534v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large-scale tensors arising in science and engineering are often too large to form or store explicitly. Their multilinear contractions, however, can frequently be evaluated efficiently, which makes randomized Frobenius-norm estimation a practical alternative to exact computation. In this paper, we study estimation of the squared Frobenius norm of a real order-$d$ tensor from such contractions using independent real, complex, or quaternion Gaussian probes. For a rank-one tensor, one normalized sample is a product of $d-1$ independent Gamma variables. This gives exact relative-variance factors $3^{d-1}-1$, $2^{d-1}-1$, and $(3/2)^{d-1}-1$, respectively. Under the same budget of underlying real Gaussian vectors, the quaternion probe has smaller rank-one variance than four independent real probes for $d\ge3$; a real-channel representation identifies the gain as modewise pooling. For orthogonal CP tensors, the exact relative variance equals the corresponding rank-one factor divided by the participation-ratio effective rank and the number of samples. For arbitrary real tensors, we prove sharp uniform moment bounds, attained at rank one, and obtain Chebyshev guarantees. A classical block-median construction then gives two-sided exponential confidence for the modified estimator. Numerical examples test the rank-one and effective-rank formulas. An implicit infinite-series kernel tensor illustrates contraction-based norm evaluation; EEG maps provide a qualitative spatial interpolation illustration.

title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
authors: William Chen, Lior Silberman, Ury Segal, Chen Greif
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12608v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.

title: Optimal Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities under different relaxations of bounded variance assumption
authors: Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with $m$ workers, $K$ oracle calls per worker per round, and $N$ rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from $(KN)^{-1/2}$ to $(KN)^{-1}$ with local steps and from $(mKN)^{-1/2}$ to $(mKN)^{-1}$ with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in $m$. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over $KN$ sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all $mKN$ samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an $N^{-2}$ gradient term, a $(KN)^{-1}$ monotone term, and a $(mKN)^{-1}$ sampling term, without assuming SGC.

title: Median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for nested integration
authors: Arved Bartuska, Yang Liu, Ra\'{u}l Tempone
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nested integrals $\int f\left(\int g(\boldsymbol{y},\boldsymbol{x})\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{x}\right)\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{y}$ where $\boldsymbol{y}\in[0,1]^{d_1}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\in[0,1]^{d_2}$ frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate $\alpha+3/2-\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon>0$ can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.

title: Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
authors: Nhat Trung Nguyen, Ivan Dorofeev, Irina Podlipnova, Yuriy Dorn, Alexander Gasnikov
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.

title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.

title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12678v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
authors: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12697v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.

title: Pointwise H\"older continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise H\"older continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise H\"older continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.

title: SDDP has polynomial iteration complexity in the horizon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12713v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) and its variants are run in practice with forward passes that sample the noise at random. Recent iteration-complexity results favour another choice: when the trial points are selected deterministically, for instance along the scenario with the largest gap, the number of iterations is polynomial in the horizon $T$, whereas every bound we know of for randomly sampled forward passes is exponential in $T$. We show that this is not intrinsic to random sampling, for a broad class of trajectory-following dynamic programming algorithms, which includes SDDP, stochastic dual dynamic integer programming and stochastic Lipschitz dynamic programming. With random sampling, and with Lipschitz constants, diameters and per-stage loss ranges bounded independently of the stage and of the horizon, the expected number of iterations whose policy is not $T\varepsilon$-optimal is $O(T\varepsilon^{-(d+1)})$, where $d$ is the state dimension: linear in $T$, as for deterministic selection rules. The proof needs no particular scenario to be sampled: the gap between the expected cost of the current policy and the current lower bound equals the expected sum of one-step Bellman residuals along the sampled path, and Lipschitz cuts that are tight at the visited states turn the positive residuals into permanent increases of a bounded potential. The results extend to noise without finite support, to backward passes on a sample average approximation, and to stationary and periodic infinite-horizon SDDP with geometric pass lengths.

title: Childcare Waitlists
authors: Yueyang Zhong, Jun Li, Senthil Veeraraghavan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity.
  We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.

title: Minimax Rates for Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12740v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the two-sample estimation of the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional under projected $r$-th moment assumptions. Let $N=n\wedge m$, where $n$ and $m$ are two sample sizes. We establish the minimax rates in the noncritical regimes. When $p<2p$, the minimax risk is of order $N^{-(r-p)/r}$, while for $r>2p$ it is of order $N^{-1/2}$. In both cases, the natural plug-in estimator is minimax rate-optimal. At the endpoint $r=p$, the minimax risk is bounded away from zero, so uniformly consistent estimation is impossible. At the critical order $r=2p$, we obtain the exact worst-case rate of the plug-in estimator and a lower bound for the minimax risk, leaving a logarithmic gap between the lower and upper bounds. The exact minimax rate in this critical case remains open.

title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12745v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$.
  For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12784v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.

title: Reflexivity of Grothendieck Spaces and Strongly Normal Sequences
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12787v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A normalized sequence $(y_n)$ in the dual $E^{*}$ of a Banach space $E$ is called normal if it is weak-star null, and strongly normal if [ G(y_n)=\left{x\in E:\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n(x)|<\infty\right} ] is dense in $E$. We prove that, within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, reflexivity is characterized by the subsequence behavior of normal sequences: a Grothendieck space $E$ is reflexive if and only if every normal sequence in $E^{*}$ contains a strongly normal subsequence. If $E$ is nonreflexive and Grothendieck, then $E^{*}$ contains a normalized weakly null sequence none of whose subsequences is strongly normal; more strongly, it contains a closed hereditarily $\ell_{1}$ subspace $Y$ with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis such that no sequence in $S(Y)$ is strongly normal. We also obtain an exact quotient criterion valid for arbitrary Banach spaces: a normal sequence has a strongly normal subsequence precisely when, for some subsequence $z=(z_n)$, the quotient $E/\bigcap_n\ker z_n$ is separable. The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson--Maurey--Schechtman and Popov. Concrete realizations are given in $(L_{\infty}(\mu))^{*}$ for nonatomic probability spaces (and, more generally, for $\sigma$-finite spaces with a nonatomic part) and in $\ell_{\infty}^{*}$.

title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carath\'eodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12797v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a Carath\'eodory-type extension theorem for premeasures with values in general separated abelian net convergence groups. Starting from hereditary exhaustivity on the source ring and intrinsic conditions for combining null errors, we construct a countably additive extension on a regulated Boolean sigma-algebra, with full upper and lower regularity in the original convergence. Completeness is required only on the limit-stable hull of the source range. Under closed summation for arbitrary directed rows and finite-response reflection, we identify the regulated domain with the splitting class of Sion's inner and outer processes. For a Dedekind-complete real vector lattice, we show that sequential closed summation on a bounded interval is equivalent to weak sigma-distributivity of the generated band, giving a converge-theoretic interpretation of the concept. Source representations allow us to recover the partially ordered-group extension of Volauf and the finite-variation extension of Kusraev and Malyugin from the general theorem. We then treat finite semivariation by adjoining dominated coordinate variations to an additive lift of the premeasure. The resulting extension is defined on the full semivariation regulator domain and preserves semivariation exactly, without requiring decomposability or the countable sup property. It includes measures of infinite vector variation.

title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12821v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.

title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12833v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.

title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
authors: Kui Ji, Chunlan Jiang, Zhenyue Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12857v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.

title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
authors: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender, Andrea Lodi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12876v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.

title: Numerical Smoothness and Error Analysis for Evolution Equations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12888v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This is a lecture note to introduce the innovative concept of numerical smoothness and its application in the error analysis of numerical solutions of evolution equations. We start from the two fundamentally different error splittings. One splitting is popular, which brings us to local error defined along the original solution and error propagation by numerical schemes. The well know Lax Equivalence Theorem is based on this error splitting. The other splitting can only be seen in a few numerical ODE books, which brings us to local error defined along the numerical solution and error propagation by the solutions of the evolution equations. The innovative concept of numerical smoothness arises from the second error splitting. While there are many difficulties when we use numerical stability in error analysis of nonlinear evolution equations, we will show that numerical smoothness works naturally in error analysis/estimation/control with advantages in several ways. We will define temporal and spatial numerical smoothness indicators, prove the necessity of the boundedness of these indicators for having optimal convergence rate, and show computable error estimates as functions of these smoothness indicators. Moreover, these error estimates are optimal in the approximatons' convergence rates and also optimal in the error propagation of the evolution equation. In comparison with error analysis framework of the Lax Equivalence Theorem, from the necessity results and the error estimates proven in the numerical smoothness framework, we have a new equivalence theory: Consistency + Numerical Smoothness <=> optimal error estimates. Unlike the Lax Equivalence Theorem, the new equivalence theory works well for nonlinear problems, nonlinear schemes, and many other complications of problems.

title: When is Hotelling's $T^2$ asymptotically $F$-distributed?
authors: Yanpeng Li, Guangming Pan, Wang Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For Gaussian observations, a deterministic multiple of Hotelling's $T^2$ statistic has an exact $F$ distribution. This paper investigates when this approximation remains valid for an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data matrix $\mathbf{X}\in \mathbb{R}^{p\times n}$ with a fixed, possibly heavy-tailed entry law $\xi$. Under symmetry and $\limsup_{n\rightarrow \infty} p/n<1$, we prove that approximation by the $F$ distribution in Kolmogorov distance is equivalent to belonging to the domain of attraction of the normal law. Both conditions are equivalent to relative concentration of the diagonal entries of the null-space projection $\mathbf{P}=\mathbf{I}_n-\mathbf{X}^{\top}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\top})^{-1}\mathbf{X}$. The central quantity $R=\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{1}$ measures the geometric alignment between the averaging direction and the random row space of $\mathbf{X}$. For symmetric finite-variance entries, the sufficient approximation extends to every sequence $1\le px)=0$ when $p/n\rightarrow \gamma\in (0,1)$, and obtain the $F$ approximation as a consequence. Centered standardized Pareto laws show that the exponent $5/2$ is sharp for this universal absolute-tail sufficient condition, although balanced-tail nonsymmetric laws can retain the approximation at the boundary, which reveals that the asymmetry of the tails matters for the $F$ approximation.

title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.

title: A volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization
authors: Wei Gong, Zhenmin Zhang, Shengfeng Zhu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12922v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topology optimization typically involves a geometric volume/mass constraint due to the limited use of material. As a popular technique for topology optimization, the level-set method typically employs the Lagrange method, the penalty method, or the augmented Lagrangian approach to address the volume constraint. This requires careful parameter tuning and may lead to non-monotonic changes in the objective. In this paper, we present a new volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization. By imposing a scalar weighted volume?compatibility constraint in a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem, the velocity is made volume compatible at the beginning of each frozen transport interval. At the continuous level, we prove that the initial rate of change of the regularized volume vanishes and that the subsequent frozen-velocity drift is of order $T^2$; under a narrow-band assumption, the corresponding constant is independent of the smoothing parameter. For the discontinuous Galerkin spatial semi-discretization of the level-set transport equation, we derive a quantitative regularized-volume drift estimate that displays the dependence on the smoothing parameter, spatial mesh size, transport time, and discrete velocity. The effectiveness of the present algorithm is demonstrated through the minimum compliance problem for linear elasticity, the eigenfrequency maximization for structural vibration, and the minimum energy dissipation problem for Stokes flows.

title: On Eigenvector Statistics of Large-Dimensional Sample Covariance Matrices with Applications
authors: Weiming Li, Zeng Li, Qinwen Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12928v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the eigenvector-weighted spectral statistics \[
  T_n(\varphi,g)=p^{-1}tr\{\varphi(\boldsymbol{S}_n)g(\boldsymbol{\Sigma})\} \] of large-dimensional sample covariance matrices \(\boldsymbol{S}_n\) with population covariance \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\). These statistics combine functions of sample eigenvalues with sample--population eigenvector overlaps and arise in statistical losses that depend on both. As the dimension and sample size grow proportionally, we establish a joint central limit theorem for \(\{T_n(\varphi_a,g_a)\}_{a=1}^r\) with multiple analytic test functions and population weights, centered by finite-dimensional deterministic equivalents. A key intermediate step is a joint Gaussian process limit for the weighted resolvent traces \[
  m_n^g(z)=p^{-1}tr\{(\boldsymbol{S}_n-z\boldsymbol{I}_p)^{-1}g(\boldsymbol{\Sigma})\}. \] The limiting means and cross-covariances are expressed in terms of the population spectral distribution. We apply these results in two settings: one concerns the variance component of minimum-norm prediction risk, and the other concerns the Frobenius loss of fixed rotationally invariant covariance estimators. For fixed affine shrinkage rules, the loss means, variances, and cross-covariances have explicit formulas in terms of population spectral moments.

title: Linear and entropy-stable scheme for the dynamic van der Waals model of non-isothermal liquid-vapor flows
authors: Yunzhuo Guo, Zhonghua Qiao, Xianmin Xu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13029v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear and decoupled fully discrete scheme that preserves the entropy production property for the dynamic van der Waals model. This model provides a thermodynamically consistent diffuse-interface framework for describing non-isothermal phase transitions in single-component liquid-vapor systems, containing the coupled conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy. We first introduce an equivalent reformulation of the governing equations that avoids the use of chain-rule identities, which generally fail under discrete differentiation. Further, a component-wise convex-splitting method is employed to calculate the discrete chemical potential and temperature. This treatment provides a discrete entropy-stable inequality without a time step restriction. Based on the explicitly treated velocity, the scheme allows the three conservation equations to be solved linearly and sequentially in a decoupled manner. Since the momentum equation does not directly affect the entropy-stability analysis, we use a classical linear semi-implicit scheme to solve it. Numerical experiments verify the expected numerical accuracy. Simulations of droplet evaporation and two- and three-dimensional Leidenfrost effects further demonstrate the proposed method can capture complex non-isothermal phase-transition dynamics while numerically reproducing the discrete entropy production behavior.

title: Beyond Hypercontractivity: Stronger Communication Converses via R\'enyi Contraction
authors: Ryo Hommura Moore, Amedeo Roberto Esposito
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13030v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the relationship between strong data-processing inequalities for R\'enyi divergences and hypercontractivity. For R\'enyi divergences of order greater than one, we characterize the contraction of R\'enyi divergences through a property of the dual Markov operator that we name power contraction. Using the contraction coefficient, we derive an upper bound on rectangle probabilities in terms of their marginals that is at least as strong as the corresponding bound obtained via hypercontractivity. Combining this result with inversion of the binary R\'enyi divergence, we derive communication lower bounds for one-way communication-assisted agreement distillation. Examples involving binary symmetric and rare-event Z-channels illustrate the improvements over standard hypercontractive converses.

title: Uniform Exponential Attractors for Non-Autonomous Dynamical Systems and an Application to the damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic growth
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we develop an abstract framework for the theory of uniform exponential attractors in non-autonomous dynamical systems. Our construction employs time-dependent absorbing sets while ensuring exponential attraction among the constructed sets. Moreover, we show that the resulting exponential attractors are uniform-that is, they remain stable under perturbations. As an application of this abstract theory, we study the weakly damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity. Using the proposed approach, we construct exponential attractors for the process generated by the Shatah-Struwe solution, which satisfies both energy and Strichartz estimates. Furthermore, we establish the Holder continuity of these exponential attractors with respect to the external forcing term.

title: A Palais-Smale type condition for optimal control problems
authors: Jean-Michel Coron, Li Deng, Xu Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13070v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider an optimal control problem with a general control constraint and a fixed initial state, for which convexity assumptions are absent. To establish the existence of optimal pairs, we introduce a control version of the Palais-Smale type condition adapted from critical point theory and prove that optimal pairs exist under this condition (see Theorem 2.1). Subsequently, we verify that a specific class of optimal control problems satisfies our Palais-Smale type condition (see Proposition 2.1). Furthermore, as an application, we present an example (Example 3.1) and show that, to the best of our knowledge, no existing result can be applied to establish the existence of an optimal pair in this case (see Section 3.1.1). Example 3.2 shows that finitely many Pontryagin maximum principle candidates do not guarantee the existence of an optimal control. Finally, Example 3.3 demonstrates that the proposed Palais-Smale type condition is sufficient, but not necessary, for the existence of optimal controls.

title: Tight Guarantees for Static Policies in Vehicle Sharing Networks
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study pricing in a vehicle sharing network with $N$ locations and $C$ vehicles, motivated by on-demand bike, scooter, and car sharing, as well as robotaxi and ride sharing services. Customers request directed trips between locations, with travel times following general distributions, and leave without service if no vehicle is available. Pricing affects both demand for trips and the distribution of vehicles across locations. Computing an optimal dynamic pricing policy is challenging because the system state depends on the number of vehicles available at each location and in transit (including how long they have been traveling), motivating the use of simple static policies that offer a fixed price for each trip.
  For any number of vehicles and locations, we establish a tight performance guarantee for static pricing relative to optimal dynamic pricing. The guarantee holds for any concave objective functions (including revenue rate) and general travel time distributions. Our tight guarantee is bounded below by $ \frac{C}{C + \min \{ C -1, \sqrt{ CN} \} }$ (over 50%), achieving the first universal, non-asymptotic constant factor guarantee. We also prove that the optimal static policy can be efficiently computed by solving a convex optimization problem. Finally, we extend our performance guarantee to the setting with supply redirection.

title: A Lipschitz refinement of the Bebutov-Kakutani dynamical embedding theorem for connected Lie group actions
authors: Yonatan Gutman, Qiang Huo, Kangbo Ouyang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13091v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected Lie group equipped with a compatible right-invariant metric and let $G$ act continuously on a compact metrizable space $X$. We prove that $X$ admits a $G$-equivariant embedding into the right argument shift action on the space of one-Lipschitz maps from $G$ to $[0,1]$ if and only if the set of fixed points topologically embeds into $[0,1]$. This generalizes a theorem proved by Gutman, Huo and Tsukamoto for $\mathbb{R}^k$-flows.

title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.

title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13100v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.

title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface
authors: Nima Chaharbaghi, Florian Kaltenberger, Bartosz Podrygajlo, Rakesh Mundlamuri, Roberto Verdone
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.

title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13141v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.

title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
authors: Yoshiaki Inoue, Michel Mandjes, Liron Ravner
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13142v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

title: Hausdorff Dimension and Flexibility for Attractors of Non-Uniformly Hyperbolic Flows
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of attracting sets of three-dimensional flows whose one-dimensional quotient dynamics is non-uniformly expanding. Our main assumption is that the quotient map admits a full-branch uniformly expanding Gibbs--Markov induced map. We first prove that every such attractor contains a hyperbolic horseshoe of Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than two. As a consequence, after an arbitrarily small $C^2$ perturbation, the associated dynamical Lagrange and Markov spectra have robustly non-empty interior for an open and dense set of $C^1$-observables. We then establish intermediate dimension properties. Every admissible intermediate Hausdorff dimension is realized by an ergodic invariant measure supported on the attractor. Moreover, every intermediate stable and unstable dimension is realized by a strictly ergodic hyperbolic subsystem. The approach extends the dimension theory previously developed for geometric Lorenz attractors to more general non-uniformly hyperbolic attractors including singular-hyperbolic attractors, Rovella attractors, and broad classes of skew-product suspension flows modeled by intermittent and Benedicks--Carleson maps.

title: Haar measure for totally positive split real semisimple quantum groups of classical type
authors: Kenny De Commer, Geoffrey Janssens, Wannes Malfait
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13213v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\hbar$ be a non-zero real number and put $q= e^{-\pi i \hbar}$. Let $G$ be a semisimple split real Lie group of classical type, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and associated Borel subalgebra $\mathfrak{b} \subseteq \mathfrak{g}$. We show that there exists a locally compact quantum group $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$ which integrates the Borel part $U_q(\mathfrak{b})$ of the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, viewed as a Hopf $*$-algebra. We further compute the associated Haar weights and modular data for $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$. Up to an excess Cartan part, the Drinfeld double of $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$ can be seen as an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup $G^+\subseteq G$.

title: Numerical Stability of Extended-Domain Spectral Collocation: Floating-Point Regularization and an Equilibrium Law for the Frame Constants
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13222v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extended-domain spectral collocation expands the solution of a boundary value problem in the Laplacian eigenbasis of an enclosing box and collocates at as many nodes as modes. The square system is exponentially ill-conditioned, and the impossibility theorem for equispaced data rules out stable geometric convergence; yet such solvers converge geometrically to a few orders of magnitude above the unit roundoff. We explain why in one dimension. The collocation solution is the solution operator applied to the interpolant of the data in an operator-dependent test space whose Lebesgue constant must grow exponentially for geometric convergence, so exact solutions can amplify data errors exponentially. In floating-point arithmetic the error of any coefficient vector is bounded by its nodal residual, its distance to a competitor and two frame constants, a leakage and a restricted Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund constant, bounded uniformly in the number of modes at a fixed positive threshold; for a backward-stable solve, under a condition on the perturbed matrix, the bound is uniform in the conditioning for suitably analytic data and, with computed constants, within a factor of about ten of the error floor of a direct solver. For the Poisson operator the rate of the two constants along the tail of the spectrum is given by a constrained equilibrium problem of logarithmic potential theory. For an interval of length $L$ extended by $\delta$ at each end, the problems for $\delta$ and $L^2/(4\delta)$ are dual, the rate is linear for $\delta = L/2$, and it starts with slope minus the fraction of the extended domain occupied by the extension, so for $\delta < L/2$ the leakage constant obeys no power law with the exponent of the end of the spectrum. In experiments, convection--diffusion operators behave like the Poisson operator at moderate P\'eclet numbers.

title: ADER-ZIST - a mixed explicit ADER-DG and zonally implicit space-time DG approach for Cartesian cut cell meshes
authors: Michael Dumbser, Christian Engwer, Sandra May, Peter Munch
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present high order accurate mixed explicit-implicit discontinuous Galerkin (DG) schemes for the solution of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws on Cartesian cut cell meshes. Such meshes may contain arbitrarily small cut cells, which leads to the well-known small cell problem: the CFL condition of explicit schemes would severely restrict the admissible time step. To overcome this difficulty, we use high order explicit fully-discrete one-step ADER-DG schemes only on Cartesian cells away from the embedded boundaries. The zone close to the embedded boundary, which consists of cut cells and their direct face neighbors, is discretized with an implicit space-time DG scheme that is coupled to the explicit scheme directly via the numerical flux. The resulting scheme, called ADER-ZIST (ADER-DG with Zonally Implicit Space-Time DG), is conservative by construction, and its time step is determined only by the size of the Cartesian background cells. Curved embedded boundaries are represented by high order isoparametric sub-triangles inside the cut cells, and the nonlinear system of the implicit cells is solved via an inexact matrix-free Newton-Krylov method. For problems with shock waves, we add an artificial viscosity term whose strength is controlled by an oscillation-eliminating smoothness sensor. ADER-ZIST is assessed on a comprehensive set of test problems for the compressible Euler equations, ranging from smooth flows around straight and curved embedded boundaries to acoustic scattering and shock-dominated flows. The scheme essentially reaches its nominal order of accuracy N+1 for smooth solutions and for polynomial degrees up to N=5, on meshes with minimal volume fractions of the small cut cells down to the order of 10^-7.

title: Dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms I: Stationary measures
authors: Weikun He, Yuxiang Jiao, Disheng Xu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a structure theorem for smooth random walks on the circle and study the dimensional properties of their stationary measures, including exact dimensionality and a Ledrappier-Young-type dimension formula. These results provide the technical tools needed for the main theorems in Part II "Dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms II: Minimal sets". They also yield an approximation theorem in the spirit of Katok, Avila-Crovisier-Wilkinson, and Morris-Shmerkin, together with a time-reversal symmetry for circle actions: every semigroup $T$ contained in $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+\alpha}(\mathbb{S}^1)$ without finite orbits has the same number of minimal sets as its inverse semigroup $T^{-1}$.

title: On Surjective Max-Phase Isometries of Schatten p-Classes (0<p<1)
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate max-phase isometries on Schatten quasi-classes in the range $0

<1$. Motivated by the rigidity theory for smooth normed spaces [\emph{Results Math.} \textbf{80} (2025), Article 126], we establish its operator-theoretic counterpart in the quasi-Banach setting. We prove that every surjective max-phase isometry on a finite-dimensional Schatten class is a standard real-linear Schatten isometry multiplied by an even sign-valued function, without any continuity assumption. This extends the scope of the classical Schatten isometry classification [\emph{Proc. Edinburgh Math. Soc.} \textbf{37} (1994), 239--242] to nonlinear mappings preserving only unsigned two-point metric data. Our approach combines support orthogonality, a symmetrized rank-one spectral formula, and a max-profile uniqueness principle. For arbitrary Hilbert spaces, we obtain the corresponding classification on finite-rank operators, while continuity yields the full-space result. We also establish preservation of rank, singular values, and two-sided support orthogonality.

title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
authors: Tan H. Cao, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Trang Nguyen, Thi Phung
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13327v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. This approach leads us to considering a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, which are reduced in turn to nondynamic mathematical programs with special types of geometric and functional constraints. Invoking powerful tools of first-order and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation, we derive necessary optimality conditions for discrete-time and then---by passing to the limit over the diminishing step of discretization---continuous-time controlled sweeping processes. A crucial role in our device is played by explicit coderivative evaluations of set-valued mapping associated with the sweeping dynamics. In this way, we establish novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes that contain absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local and global maximization conditions, $L^2$ active set multipliers, vector measures generated by sweeping and control constraints, and free-time transversality condition expressed through the averaged Hamiltonian. For suitably selected multipliers, we also obtain nondegenerate forms of these conditions when the optimal trajectory starts on the boundary of the moving set. The efficiency of the obtained results is illustrated by some examples related to practical modeling.

title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
authors: Lukas Pflug, Michael Stingl, Max Zetzmann
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13355v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show the convergence of a commonly used mesh-free discretization of a dynamic non-linear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage implemented via a bond-breakage criterion for a fixed horizon $\delta >0$. The model chosen here is a mathematically well-posed regularization of a discontinuous peridynamic operator often found in the literature, which assumes that fracture results from strain in tension only. We explicitly include the one-point quadrature used in this scheme in the analysis. The convergence is with respect to the natural norm of the solution space given by $C^1([0,T],L^\infty(\Omega)^d)$, and therefore $L^\infty(\Omega)^d$ in the spatial coordinates. This result heavily constrains the spatial regularity of the continuous solution which we prove afterwards. More specifically, for locally $L$-Lipschitz continuous input data, local Lipschitz bounds are derived for the displacement, regardless of damage. This is consistent with interpreting the peridynamic model used here as an approximation to a truly discontinuous fracture model with a length-scale parameter given by the horizon $\delta>0$. We note that we do not deal with the limit of the solutions as $\delta \searrow 0$.

title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert--Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.

title: Banach space, Birkhoff--James orthogonality, James constant, von Neumann--Jordan constant
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13360v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Mart\'in, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45].
  Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.

title: Finite-Sample Bounds for Fr\'echet Means of Dependent Data in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove finite-sample risk bounds for empirical quadratic and power Fr\'echet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above for observations with arbitrary joint law. We compare the sample with exchangeable copies in which one observation is redrawn independently of the original sample and the others move to preserve the joint law. These displacements control the error, with no entropy or dimension assumptions. For quadratic Fr\'echet means, this yields a general ``coupling bound'' in any separable complete $CAT(\kappa)$ space, where for $\kappa>0$ the observations must lie in a closed convex set of circumradius below $\pi/(2\sqrt{\kappa})$. This bound is exact on the real line for nonnegatively correlated Gaussian observations and for comonotone functions of a common factor. We apply it in two settings. Under local dependence, the resulting risk bound grows linearly with the average size of the dependency neighborhoods. Under transport sensitivity and for bounded metric variances, summable sensitivities of the conditional laws to a change in one observation preserve the parametric mean squared error rate, while nonsummable polynomial decay gives explicit slower rates. We verify transport sensitivity for stationary reversible Markov chains with Wasserstein-contractive kernels and for bi-Lipschitz images of Gaussian sequences. In the more challenging setting of heavy-tailed, dependent data with possibly infinite variance, we consider power Fr\'echet means of order $\alpha\in(1,2)$. Under nonpositive curvature, we bound their $L^\alpha$ risk assuming only finite $\alpha$-th moments.

title: On the simultaneous zero inclusion property and characterization of Inner product space
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13378v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that if a Banach space $X$ is smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund and if satisfies the following \[0\in W(T) \implies 0\in W(T^{-1})\] for all invertible bounded linear map on $X$ then Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $X$ is symmetric. This result, therefore, characterizes the inner product spaces out of all smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces having three or more dimension via simultaneous zero inclusion property, introduced by Bra\v{c}i\v{c} et al. [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 449 (2017) 1413-1423]. Further, this gives answers to some open questions asked by E. Poon [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 534(2024), 128052].
